messages:
Meera: quick heads-up — after the routing change last night we are seeing higher p95 on a subset of requests. suspect edge routing + quantized kernel combo. can we triage?
Alex: saw this too, flagged from our synthetic job. p50 roughly same, p95 jumps in eu-west and us-west for int8 runs.
John: timeline — routing rollout @ 03:10 UTC, traffic shift to nearest POP, fallback policy updated to prefer regional cheaper pools.
Marie: posting quick numbers from the 1am perf-run (50k requests, seq=512, batch target 8):
```
Model: rw-open-13B-quant-int8
GPU: A100
us-east  p50=36ms  p95=92ms  tokens/s=420
us-west  p50=39ms  p95=210ms tokens/s=400
eu-west  p50=45ms  p95=260ms tokens/s=380

Model: rw-open-13B-fp16
GPU: A100
us-east  p50=34ms  p95=78ms  tokens/s=430
us-west  p50=38ms  p95=95ms  tokens/s=410
eu-west  p50=41ms  p95=110ms tokens/s=400
```
Marie: note the int8 p95 spike only in non-us-east regions.
Meera: interesting — so quantization + region = regressions. could be kernel selection or cold JITs. any kernel logs?
perf-bot: kernel-selection-report for run 2024-04-01T01:02:
```
us-east  -> kernel=flash_attn_v2 optimized, compiled=true, compile-ms=12
us-west  -> kernel=cutlass_variant fallback, compiled=false, runtime-ms=48
eu-west  -> kernel=triton_fused fallback, compiled=false, runtime-ms=62
```
Alex: that matches: us-east got flash_attn fast path. other regions are hitting fallback kernels with higher per-step runtime and sometimes triggering extra kernel warmups.
John: also saw network traces — some requests from us-west were routed to eu-west pool due to capacity, adding ~40ms RTT tail for those flows. combined with slower kernels explains p95.
Kai: quick checklist of hypotheses: 1) kernel mismatch (flash vs cutlass/triton) 2) cross-pop routing adding RTT 3) cold kernel JITs 4) batching/timeouts causing queueing.
Meera: agreed. propose experiments (short):
- force kernel policy to "prefer-flash" in us-west/eu-west for rw-open-13B-int8 and rerun
- pin a small canary of traffic to local-only pools to remove cross-pop fallback
- run a cold->warm sweep to measure compile overhead separately
- evaluate fp16 vs int8 p95 delta at same routing
Alex: implemented first two as flags, kicked off 10k synthetic each in all regions with identical seeds.
perf-bot: run-id 2024-04-01T01:30: forced-kernel=flash_attn_v2, local-only=true, batch_target=8, seq=512
Marie: new numbers (forced flash):
```
Model: rw-open-13B-quant-int8 (forced flash)
GPU: A100
us-east  p50=35ms p95=88ms tokens/s=425
us-west  p50=36ms p95=94ms tokens/s=420
eu-west  p50=40ms p95=96ms tokens/s=410
```
Marie: huge improvement. p95 collapse to ~100ms across regions.
John: confirms cross-pop routing was amplifying the issue: local-only runs eliminated extra RTTs.
Meera: good signal — looks like two contributors: kernel selection + routing. next: why were non-us-east regions not picking flash_attn by default?
Alex: kernel selector uses a heuristic: prefer flash when estimated memory per-block <= threshold AND kernel binary available on node. rollout of flash kernels had been staged and not present in some european nodes (packaging bug).
Kai: Ops note: packaging missed lightweight kernel bundle for eu-west-2. tracked as infra ticket INF-2421.
Meera: action items:
- Alex: revert routing rollback? or better: update selector to prefer flash if available and trigger pre-warm fetch of kernel bundle (due EOD)
- John: add soft-capacity buffer to avoid cross-pop fallback for small bursts (2-3 extra instances)
- Marie: run longer mixed workload (100k requests, varying seq 32..1024) to ensure no regression on throughput
- Kai: patch packaging to include kernel bundles in eu nodes + smoke test
Alex: I'll also add a metric in Console: kernel_path_used + compile_time_ms per-pop so we can alert when fallback path is used frequently.
Meera: one more datapoint — H100 (in dedicated pools) didn't show as bad even with int8 fallbacks: p95 in all regions ~85-110ms. likely GPU microarchitecture + kernel variants. we'll include H100 in the mixed run.
Marie: final note: quantization still gives ~15% tokens/s win vs fp16 with no quality issues in evals. so we want int8 but must ensure consistent kernel availability and route locality.
Meera: thanks team — let's sync in 30 to review extended run. I'll update thread with failures if any. :thumbsup:
